free_tier.stated: The entry shape is KRW 9,000 a month including VAT for 1 GB RAM, 30 GB SSD and 300 GB of monthly traffic. Above it: 16,000 for 2 GB and 40 GB and 500 GB, 22,000 for 3 GB and 50 GB and 800 GB, 33,000 for 4 GB and 100 GB and 1.2 TB, 55,000 for 6 GB and 150 GB and 1.5 TB. Every plan carries a KRW 22,000 setup fee and an overage charge of KRW 165 per GB.

record.interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
record.chaining: Cafe24 is the only Korean host found that sells a real Linux VM at KRW 9,000 including tax with no minimum term; it does not chain, because the 300 GB allowance and the KRW 165 per GB overage make it a host for a small service rather than a data mover.

limits.value: 300 GB of monthly traffic on the entry plan, then KRW 165 per GB; the overage is the expensive part, because 1 TiB above the allowance would cost more than the server, so the volume quota fails long before the CPU does.

record.notes: The vCPU count is not on the plan table, so it is left null rather than guessed. Cafe24 raised the entry price from KRW 7,000 to 9,000 on the day a Korean trade paper reported, citing SSD and memory cost; the raise is a reliability fact about the Korean floor, not a defect. The setup fee is the detail that changes the arithmetic for a one-month test: KRW 22,000 is more than two months of the server itself.
